title: Jeroboam’s political craft: minimize religious change so ten tribes stay—cannot have swapped Jehovah for Apis
source_text: XXXIII. Et certe, cum cultus ille vitulorum, ut ex Scriptura sacra manifeste colligitur, a Rege Jeroboam fuerit astu quodam excogitatus, ut, scilicet, subditis suis non amplius esset necesse Hierosolymam proficisci, ad solemnem cultum Deo exhibendum, ne frequens istud cum urbe Jerusalem commercium, occasio ipsis esset in gratiam cum Domo Davidica redeundi, proculdubio, modo finem illum obtineret, in recepta religione quam minimum immutavit, ne subditorum suorum animos a se alienaret. Religionem autem, apud decem tribus ipsi adhaerentes receptam, non simpliciter immutasset, sed funditus subvertisset, si Jehovae Dei Israelis cultu penitus abrogato, pro summo Deo populo suo proposuisset, vel bovem Aegyptium, vel vituli figuram nuper a se fabricatam.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly, since that cult of the calves, as is manifestly gathered from Holy Scripture, was devised by King Jeroboam by a certain craft, that, namely, it might no longer be necessary for his subjects to set out to Jerusalem, to exhibit solemn cult to God, lest that frequent commerce with the city Jerusalem be for them an occasion of returning into favor with the House of David, without doubt, provided he obtained that end, he changed as little as possible in the received religion, lest he alienate the minds of his subjects from himself. But the religion received among the ten tribes adhering to him he would not simply have changed, but would have overturned from the foundation, if, the cult of Jehovah the God of Israel being utterly abrogated, he had proposed to his people for the highest God either the Egyptian ox, or a figure of a calf newly fabricated by himself.
pass_b_english: Jeroboam’s aim was political: stop Jerusalem pilgrimages without revolting the tribes.
Swapping Jehovah for Apis or a brand-new calf-god would have been religious overthrow, not crafty minimal change.

choices.why: Political rival Jeroboam feared Jerusalem would restore.
